title: PowerShell Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: Write-Output sends a value to the output stream. Here it appears in the terminal.

examples.title: Keep a named value
examples.description: PowerShell variable names start with a dollar sign.

examples.title: Build a message
examples.description: Double-quoted strings expand variables inside the text.

examples.title: Choose an action
examples.description: -ge compares numbers using greater-than-or-equal. if chooses a block.

examples.title: Read an array item
examples.description: An array holds several values. Its first index is zero.

examples.title: Visit every item
examples.description: foreach runs its block for each value in a group.

examples.title: Read a named key
examples.description: A hashtable pairs keys with values. Brackets select a value by key.

examples.title: Make named properties
examples.description: A custom object groups properties. Dot notation reads a property.

examples.title: Filter pipeline values
examples.description: Where-Object keeps values that pass a rule. $_ means the current pipeline item.

examples.title: Transform pipeline values
examples.description: ForEach-Object runs a block for each incoming value.

examples.title: Name reusable steps
examples.description: A function can declare inputs with param. An unassigned expression becomes output.

examples.title: Handle a terminating error
examples.description: try and catch handle a terminating error. throw creates one here.
examples.code: try { throw "Missing score" } catch { Write-Output "Try again" }
